summary: Over the window a novel coronavirus outbreak in China escalated from a handful of reported deaths to city-wide quarantine, a national leading group, extended national holidays, and confirmed international spillover. By the final days the disruption had reached global supply of travel and consumer activity (border closures, resort shutdowns, a quarantined cruise ship in Italy, a quarantined evacuation flight into the US), which is the kind of broad, open-ended economic shock that would plausibly reprice risk and lift volatility.
mechanism: An escalating epidemic in a major manufacturing and consumption economy transmits to markets through expected demand destruction, travel/consumption shutdowns and supply-chain interruption, while the unbounded uncertainty about the infection curve widens the distribution of outcomes and raises implied and realised volatility.

claims.claim: Chinese authorities reported a third death from the coronavirus and confirmed spread from Wuhan to Shenzhen, Beijing and Hong Kong.
Chinese authorities quarantined the entire city of Wuhan, suspending all public transport, as the death toll reached 17.
The reported toll escalated sharply during the window, with Hubei reporting 1,291 new confirmed cases and a cumulative 106 deaths.
Economic and consumer activity was directly curtailed: Shanghai Disney Resort closed and the Chinese government extended the Spring Festival holiday under a new leading group headed by the Premier.
Cross-border effects appeared, with North Korea banning foreign tourists and closing its border with China.

By the last two days, containment measures had spread outside Asia: over 6,000 passengers were barred from disembarking a cruise ship in Italy over two suspected cases, and a flight of 195 Americans returning from China was quarantined.
China's head of state publicly addressed the World Health Organization about defeating the virus, indicating the outbreak had become a top-level state matter.

competing_explanation: Two other candidates appear: the European Parliament's 621-49 approval of the Brexit agreement, marking Britain's last day of EU parliamentary representation, and the unveiling of the US-Israeli Middle East plan rejected by the Palestinian president. Both are macro-relevant political events, but the Brexit vote was a widely anticipated ratification of an already-signed agreement and the peace plan carried no direct financial channel, whereas the outbreak items escalate continuously and end the window with fresh, unresolved developments.
